pairs.old: The final OCM evaluation found minimal net savings to Medicare — about 0.2% of episode costs in the best-performing cohort. However, quality improvements were meaningful: participating practices showed higher hospice use, fewer ED visits, and better symptom documentation.
pairs.new: The final OCM evaluation found that total episode payments rose 2.1% less in OCM than in comparison episodes, but monthly and performance-based payments to practices outweighed those savings, leaving Medicare an estimated $639 million net loss. Practice-reported screening measures improved, but OCM had no measurable impact on ED visits, hospital stays, or hospice use relative to comparison practices.
